An Exposed Zone presents an opening for an attack (PHB v4.21, Exposed Zones):

  • Its Protection counts as 0, subject to any exception in the Attack's description (a Quick Strike's says Protection applies even to an Exposed Zone).
  • It remains Exposed until you Recenter ❶, unless the effect that Exposed it specifies another duration.
  • A Critical Hit against it with a Deliberate or Committed Strike inflicts a Wound.
  • Exposure caused by a Posture lasts until the end of the round and cannot be cleared by Recenter; Exposure caused by Control ends when that Control ends.

When a Zone is Exposed, the following condition is placed on you: Exposed [Zone Name]. Zones become Exposed when your Deliberate or Committed Strike Misses, when a Committed Strike Grazes, when you take a Posture that says so, when a foe Controls your weapon in a Bind, when a Deliberate or Committed Strike of yours lands and you choose to open the Zone it struck, and through certain Talents and critical effects.

The condition

ConditionEffect
Exposed [Zone]That Zone is Exposed: Hits can land there instead of your Torso. Protection counts as 0. Recenter ❶ to clear unless otherwise stated.

Your Speed becomes 0 until you spend an action to rise, and your Arms become Exposed.

What a Critical Hit does to each Zone, Exposed or not, is on @UUID[Compendium.starwrought.rules.JournalEntry.489b438244686d7b.JournalEntryPage.35ee7b6b93251cf3]{Zones and Critical Hits}.

In the system

Each Exposed Zone shows on the token as its own status (Exposed: Head, Exposed: Torso, Exposed: Arms, Exposed: Legs) and in the Zones panel of the sheet. Toggling the status on the token and toggling the Zone on the sheet are the same change. Recenter closes every Exposed Zone except one a Posture opened, and the statuses close with them.

A Bind forms when a rigid weapon or shield Guards against a melee Attack that Grazes or Misses, provided the implements involved can Bind (PHB v4.21, Binds): on a Graze a neutral Bind forms; on a Miss the defender gains Control of the attacking implement. Track one relationship per implement, and name the two implements: longsword / spear, or shield > bite. A Bind is neutral (/) when neither fighter has the line, or Controlled (>) when one does.

Use Gain Control ❶ to contest an existing Bind. A Parry ❶↺ that Stops a melee Strike may at once attempt to Gain Control of the attacking weapon, and a Riposte makes a Quick Strike instead.

While you Control a weapon

  • Your partner has an Exposed Zone of your choice, and it stays Exposed while the Bind lasts.
  • Your partner's attacks with the Controlled weapon take a −2 Situation penalty.
  • You may Close ❶: Step toward your partner while keeping the Bind. The Controlled weapon cannot Intercept you.

How a Bind ends

A Bind ends when a participant uses the bound implement to Strike (a Strike against the other participant resolves before the Bind ends), when either participant Moves or Steps unless an ability expressly preserves the Bind, when either participant Recenters, when a third party attacks the combatant who currently has Control, or when either bound implement is dropped or Disarmed. Control redirects an implement; it does not itself make its wielder Grabbed or Restrained. The Controlled combatant can still Move, Step, or attack with another weapon or limb, and attacking with an unbound weapon or limb ends the Bind before the attack roll.

Recenter ❶ ends every Bind you are in and clears your Exposed Zones, except those Exposed by a Posture. Exposure caused specifically by Control ends when that Control ends; Exposure from other sources follows its own duration.

Size. Creatures of the same Size, or one Size apart, Bind normally. Two or more Sizes apart, the smaller creature can gain only momentary Control: it ends after its first benefit is used or at the end of the controller's next Opportunity, whichever comes first, and the larger creature can Move without first breaking the Bind.

What cannot Bind. Unless an ability says otherwise: Flexible weapons such as whips and flails, bare hands, spells and area effects, and attacks with the Unparryable trait. Incorporeal and amorphous attackers cannot be Bound unless a rule provides a way to do so.

Third parties. An ally attacking the creature whose implement you Control does not break your Bind; a third party attacking you while you have Control does.

The conditions

ConditionEffect

If the Strike is a Graze or Miss, you may at once attempt to Gain Control of the attacking weapon.

The Zone a Controller opens follows the rules on @UUID[Compendium.starwrought.rules.JournalEntry.489b438244686d7b.JournalEntryPage.941b13c4400511a4]{Exposed}.

In the system

A Bind is recorded on both fighters and drawn on the map as a gold chain between their tokens, labelled with the two implements; a Controlled Bind runs from the Controller to the Controlled with an arrowhead and the word Control. The token carries Bound, Controlling or Controlled, and that effect names the partner, both implements and the state. The sheet's bind line and the Recenter Maneuver end it; a Strike between the two ends it when the Strike resolves.

StepDo this
1Check Immunity. Disregard damage types and effects to which the target is immune.
2Add together the applicable damage dice and modifiers for each damage type.
3Subtract the combined applicable Resistance from each damage type, to a minimum of 0. Apply Resistance once per damage type per damage instance, not once per die.
4Add applicable Weakness to each damage type that still deals damage. Independent sources of Weakness are cumulative.
5For a Zoned Attack, combine its remaining damage and subtract the struck Zone’s effective Protection once. Protection alone cannot reduce positive damage below 1. Damage already reduced to 0 remains 0.
6Double the remaining damage if the Attack’s Critical Hit rules require it.
7Apply the remaining damage to Vigor, or resolve it as the ability specifies. Apply associated effects at their stated timing.

StepDo this
1Armor and similar equipment provide Protection for the Zones they cover; a Zone with nothing worn there has 0.
2Protection reduces damage from Zoned Attacks, once per instance, and never changes the Defense roll or the Result. Protection alone cannot reduce positive damage below 1.
3Pervasive Attacks and Persistent Damage ignore ordinary Protection.
4An Exposed Zone's Protection counts as 0, subject to any exception in the Attack's description; a Critical Hit against it with a Deliberate or Committed Strike inflicts a Wound.

TraitEffect
AttackAn action a foe answers with a Defense. Attacks are resolved as Exchanges (see Chapter 4: The Exchange). A Committed Strike ❸ is also Weighted.

Some actions with the Press trait also grant an effect on a failure. The effects that are added on a failure don’t apply on a critical failure. If your Press action succeeds, you can choose to apply the failure effect instead (for example, when an attack deals no damage due to resistance).
PreparedA Maneuver of three or more actions. Spend one action now and reserve the rest; it resolves at your next Opportunity (see Encounter Mode).
PostureA special type of Reaction that doesn’t cost any actions. Any Zones Exposed by a Posture remain Exposed until the end of the round.
ReactionA Maneuver you may perform outside your Opportunity, the moment its Trigger occurs. It costs its listed actions from the same six as everything else, and you may use as many Reactions in a round as you can afford. A Reaction never triggers another Reaction. Marked ↺ beside its cost.
StanceA way of standing and holding yourself. You can be in only one stance at a time, and it lasts until you leave it, fall unconscious, or enter another.
UnparryableAn attack that cannot be answered with Parry and offers nothing to Bind. Guard still applies to it.
WeightedA Committed Strike ❸. If it is Stopped (a Graze or a Miss), you are Exposed in a Zone of the defender’s choice.
VisualIt works through sight. It fails on the blinded, and on anyone who cannot see you.
